summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of chronic venous stasis, lipodermatosclerosis, bioprosthetic aortic valve, and pacemaker was admitted for left neck redness, chills, and malaise following a TEE, concerning for cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin with rapid improvement and transitioned to oral doxycycline. During admission, she was diagnosed with recurrent C. difficile colitis based on a positive PCR, prompting initiation of a prolonged oral vancomycin course. Her warfarin dose was increased from 2 mg to 3 mg daily due to a persistently subtherapeutic INR of 1.4. She remained euvolemic on home diuretics, with stable heart failure and well-controlled atrial fibrillation. She was discharged home on oral antibiotics for both cellulitis and C. difficile, with instructions to follow up on anticoagulation and avoid loperamide until cleared by her primary care provider.
